items.headline: Stunner in Spain — Pogačar crashes out of the Vuelta while leading
items.body: The most dominant rider on the planet is out. Race leader Tadej Pogačar hit the deck hard in the peloton with about 32km to go on Stage 8, cutting his shoulder and face, and after briefly trying to remount he was helped into an ambulance — his first-ever Grand Tour DNF. Bryan Coquard won the day's sprint in Xeraco, and Spain's Enric Mas inherits the red jersey with the race blown wide open.
items.say: Did you hear Pogačar crashed out of the Vuelta while he was winning it? The best cyclist in the world, gone in one stage — first time he's ever had to quit a big tour. Whole race just got flipped.

items.headline: Liverpool rescued twice — a 2-2 draw with Forest at Anfield
items.body: Not the afternoon the champions wanted. Nottingham Forest twice went in front — Dan Ndoye's tight-angle finish, then a Morgan Gibbs-White penalty — but Liverpool clawed back both times, new signing Alexander Isak tapping in his first before Víctor Muñoz curled home a late leveller at the Kop. Alisson kept them in it; the manager called them 'lucky to only be 1-0 down' at the break.
items.say: Liverpool dropped points at home already — 2-2 with Forest, had to come from behind twice. Isak got off the mark though. You catch any of the Premier League this weekend?

items.headline: Shanghai goes wild — Song Yadong knocks out unbeaten Umar Nurmagomedov
items.body: One of the biggest upsets of the year, and in front of his home crowd. Heavy underdog Song Yadong caught the previously unbeaten Umar Nurmagomedov — cousin of the legendary Khabib — with a short right hand early in Round 2, dropping him cold and swarming for the finish at 1:48. The Chinese star just launched himself straight into the bantamweight title picture.
items.say: A Chinese fighter, Song Yadong, just knocked out Khabib's undefeated cousin in his home town — huge upset, cold in the second round. The crowd lost it. You ever watch the UFC?

items.headline: It all comes down to Sunday — $10 million and the FedExCup on the line at East Lake
items.body: The PGA Tour season ends this weekend, and it's bunched at the top. Ryan Gerard and Viktor Hovland shared the 36-hole lead at 10 under, with world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler lurking just two back — meaning Sunday's final round decides both the Tour Championship and the whole FedExCup, with a cool $10 million going to the winner.
items.say: The golf season wraps up Sunday — winner takes the FedExCup and ten million bucks, and it's a logjam with Scheffler right there. Small field, one hot round wins it. You follow golf at all?

items.headline: Williamsport crowns a champ Sunday — and there's an Ohio-vs-Nevada showdown for the U.S. title
items.body: The best week of small-ball baseball is down to the wire. Saturday sets the finals: Henderson, Nevada faces Hamilton, Ohio for the U.S. championship, while Willemstad (Curaçao) and Tokyo (Japan) play for the international crown. The two survivors meet Sunday at 3 p.m. ET for the whole thing — 12-year-olds, walk-offs and all.
items.say: The Little League World Series final is Sunday — it's honestly some of the most fun baseball all year. A team from Ohio's playing for the U.S. title. You ever get sucked into watching those kids?

items.headline: The movie Hollywood shelved finally opens — 'Coyote vs. ACME' hits theaters
items.body: A genuine underdog story: axed for a tax write-off back in 2023, then saved after fan outrage, the live-action/animated 'Coyote vs. ACME' is finally in theaters and heading for a solid low-teens-millions opening — with a shiny 95% on Rotten Tomatoes. It's the weekend's big newcomer, though Spider-Man: Brand New Day is expected to hold No. 1 for a fifth straight week.
items.say: That Coyote vs. ACME movie — the one the studio literally shelved for years before fans forced it out — finally opened, and critics love it. Wile E. Coyote suing the ACME company, Will Forte and John Cena as the lawyers. Kind of a fun redemption story.

items.headline: KATSEYE hit No. 1 — 'WILD' is the global girl group's first chart-topping album
items.body: The buzzy global pop group KATSEYE just landed their first No. 1 on the Billboard 200: their EP 'WILD' debuted on top with 170,000 units — their biggest week yet, and the biggest debut by an all-woman group of the decade. Phoebe Bridgers bowed at No. 2 right behind them. Not bad for a group only two years into the game.
items.say: You know KATSEYE? That international girl group — they just got their first No. 1 album. They kind of came out of a reality competition and blew up. The single 'Pinky Up' is everywhere. Who's on your rotation lately?

items.headline: De Niro and Adam Scott get creepy — 'The Whisper Man' lands on Netflix
items.body: A meaty new thriller to fire up this weekend: 'The Whisper Man' is out on Netflix, with Adam Scott as a widowed crime writer whose young son vanishes — pulling in his estranged father (Robert De Niro), a retired detective who once caught the serial killer now tied to the case. It's based on Alex North's bestselling novel, and it's plenty unsettling.
items.say: There's a new thriller on Netflix, The Whisper Man — De Niro and Adam Scott, a kidnapping and an old serial-killer case. Supposed to be genuinely creepy. You in the mood for something scary or do you avoid that stuff?

items.headline: TV's big night is coming — the Emmys land Sept. 14 with Mariska Hargitay hosting
items.body: Awards season for television is nearly here: the 78th Primetime Emmys air Monday, Sept. 14 on NBC and Peacock, and for the first time the host is 'Law & Order: SVU' icon Mariska Hargitay — Olivia Benson herself stepping out from behind the badge. A fun excuse to argue about the year's best shows.
items.say: The Emmys are in a couple weeks and Mariska Hargitay — Olivia Benson from SVU — is hosting, which is a great pick. Got a show you'd be rooting for? I never actually watch the ceremony but I love the debates after.
